Q: set_real_ip_from still included in HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR A:

Seems you misunderstand this nginx feature. real_ip module is for restore client address hidden to some additional header by another (front-end or load-balancing) web server.

You should remove all real_ip lines from nginx config and use X-Real-IP header in your application. If this isn't sufficient you can replace X-Forwarded-For in the server block with

proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;

Q: If: Badly formed number when using less then sign A:

The problem is that csh does not support floating points in an Expression, only integers. 

set accuracy = `cat results.dat | tail -1 | cut -c1-20`
echo '#####ACCURACY: '$accuracy
set solved = 0
if (`echo "$accuracy <= 0.000000008" | bc`) set solved = 1

For more complicated expressions one may want to use bc -l rather than plain bc. With -l things like e(x) and l(y), which implement ex and ln(y) respectively (and many more).

Note: As many have mentioned, you should avoid using csh. Despite having contributed small changes to tcsh, I have stopped using it once I read CSH Programming Considered Harmful.

Q: Imagej macro to save data generated by results and log pages into the same end excel file A:

I wrote a macro which saves results of ROI multimeasures to the log window. Since I only wanted specific results (the highest three Raw Integrated Densities), I had my code use getResult("Column Label", row) to get the results out, manipulate them, and then print to the log using print("stuff to print"). At the end, I saved the log as a csv, which one can open in excel. Just use commas to separate

Q: If product code does not exist in first part of query pull a declared value from another table for that product code A: 
SELECT 
    COALESCE(spr.Price, psb.SellPrice) AS Price, 
    Per.PerCode, 
    p.ProductCode, 
    p.Description
FROM Product p

-- get the specific customer to use in our exact pricing join
LEFT JOIN customer c 
    ON c.CustomerCode = '7000192'

-- get the specific price rule for this exact customer
LEFT JOIN SellPriceRule spr 
    ON p.ProductID = spr.ProductID 
    AND spr.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

-- get the fallback price band (Band 8 for AB region)
LEFT JOIN ProductSellPriceBand psb 
    ON p.ProductID = psb.ProductID 
    AND psb.BandNumber = 8 
    AND psb.Description LIKE 'AB%'

-- get the PerCode based on whichever table provided the price
LEFT JOIN Per 
    ON Per.PerID = COALESCE(spr.PricePerID, psb.PerID)

-- filter for the specific products you are looking for
WHERE p.ProductCode IN (
    '27MIETE10B',
    '22RGR45DHS',
    '23RGWBBCA',
    '22RGED4WA',
    '22RGED45WA'
)

It's difficult to do what you're asking for due to the lack of the original data tables.

I did it as it should be in theory. If anything's wrong, please leave a comment and I'll edit it.

Adding an aggregate function like MIN() absolutely requires grouping the rest of selected columns using a GROUP BY clause. However, there is a common trap to watch out for here: if a product happens to have two rules for the same customer with different prices, a standard GROUP BY will output a duplicate row for that product (one for each price) instead of picking the single "winning" rule.

As I see you have used [dbo] you must be using SQL Server, so there is better solution - to swap the LEFT JOIN for an OUTER APPLY:

SELECT 
    COALESCE(spr.Price, psb.SellPrice) AS Price, 
    Per.PerCode, 
    p.ProductCode, 
    p.Description,
    spr.RulePriority AS RulePrio
FROM Product p

LEFT JOIN customer c 
    ON c.CustomerCode = '7000192'

-- takes ONLY the single highest-priority rule for this product & customer
OUTER APPLY (
    SELECT TOP 1 Price, PricePerID, RulePriority
    FROM SellPriceRule
    WHERE ProductID = p.ProductID 
      AND CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    ORDER BY RulePriority ASC -- assuming lower number = higher priority
) spr

LEFT JOIN ProductSellPriceBand psb 
    ON p.ProductID = psb.ProductID 
    AND psb.BandNumber = 8 
    AND psb.Description LIKE 'AB%'

LEFT JOIN Per 
    ON Per.PerID = COALESCE(spr.PricePerID, psb.PerID)

WHERE p.ProductCode IN (
    '27MIETE10B',
    '22RGR45DHS',
    '23RGWBBCA',
    '22RGED4WA',
    '22RGED45WA'
);
